def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm) (conF : Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → Def2 𝓑 K → Def6 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 →
    Def4 𝓢 K →
    (∃ s, 𝓢 ⊢ K (s 🡘 K (F (∼s)))) →
    (∀ σ, 𝓑 ⊢ conF 🡒 ∼(F σ ⋏ F (∼σ))) →
    (∀ σ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K σ 🡒 F σ)) →
    𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF
a_raw: {"translation": "Target is the proposition asserting that for all types Fm (sentences), S₀, and S (proof systems); all structures giving Fm the object-language connectives 🡒, ⋏, ⋎, ∼ (with φ 🡘 ψ abbreviating (φ 🡒 ψ) ⋏ (ψ 🡒 φ)) and constants ⊤, ⊥; all provability relations on Fm for S₀ and S; all systems 𝓑 : S₀ and 𝓢 : S that each prove all classical propositional tautologies and are closed under modus ponens; all arbitrary functions K, F : Fm → Fm; and every sentence conF : Fm, if the following eight hypotheses all hold: (1) (Def1 𝓑 K) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓑 proves K φ; (2) (Def2 𝓑 K) for all sentences φ and ψ, 𝓑 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ); (3) (Def6 𝓑 K) for every sentence φ, 𝓑 proves K φ 🡒 K (K φ); (4) (𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢) every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (5) (Def4 𝓢 K) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K (K φ 🡒 φ); (6) there exists a sentence s : Fm such that 𝓢 proves K (s 🡘 K (F (∼s))); (7) for every sentence σ : Fm, 𝓑 proves conF 🡒 ∼(F σ ⋏ F (∼σ)); and (8) for every sentence σ : Fm, 𝓢 proves K (K σ 🡒 F σ); then 𝓢 proves ∼(K conF). Nothing further is required: in particular, neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is assumed to be consistent; 𝓢 is not assumed to satisfy Def1 (closure under φ ↦ K φ) or Def3 (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡒 φ); K and F are arbitrary functions constrained only by the listed hypotheses; conF is an arbitrary sentence constrained only by hypothesis (7); and the conclusion asserts provability of the object-language negation ∼(K conF) in 𝓢 (rather than merely that 𝓢 does not prove K conF)."}

divergences.description: The conclusion of TARGET is `𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF` (corresponding to `T ⊢ ¬B Con q`), omitting the outer `K` (`B`) of Theorem 6's conclusion `T ⊢ B¬B Con q` (which would be `𝓢 ⊢ K (∼K conF)`). Besides changing the conclusion from provable unprovability (`B¬B Con q`) to plain unprovability (`¬B Con q`), this omission makes TARGET false under its stated hypotheses: because `K φ 🡒 φ` (`Def3`) is intentionally omitted, any consistent classical system with `K φ := ⊤` and `F φ := ⊥` satisfies all hypotheses while failing to prove `∼K conF` (`∼⊤`).

Because arithmetic, Gödel numbering, and object-language quantifiers are abstracted away (as declared by the author), the fixed point `∃ s, 𝓢 ⊢ K (s 🡘 K (F (∼s)))` is assumed as a hypothesis rather than derived by the diagonal lemma, and `q(ng[s])` is rendered directly as `F (∼s)` without modelling a formula `q(x)` or the primitive recursive negation term `ng`.

`Con q`, defined in the source as the quantified arithmetic formula `∀x¬(q(x) & q(ng(x)))`, is replaced by an arbitrary sentence `conF` constrained only by the sentence-level instances `∀ σ, 𝓑 ⊢ conF 🡒 ∼(F σ ⋏ F (∼σ))` in `𝓑`, and `q(x)` is generalized to an arbitrary function `F : Fm → Fm`.

Reinhardt's single first-order arithmetic modal theory `T` (which includes arithmetic, quantifiers, and the Barcan schema `B∀xP → ∀x Bp`) is generalized to a pair of abstract classical propositional systems `𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢` with necessitation assumed only on `𝓑`, which weakens the background hypotheses on the theory.

judgement.summary: TARGET diverges materially from Reinhardt's Theorem 6 because its conclusion `𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF` drops the outer `K` (`B`) from `T ⊢ B¬B Con q`; combined with the omission of `K φ 🡒 φ`, this renders the formal statement false as written (whereas `𝓢 ⊢ K (∼K conF)` would match the theorem). Aside from this major error, the remaining differences are minor idealizations stemming from the declared abstraction away from arithmetic, Gödel numbering, and quantifiers.
